title: Kuma monitor `http: vault` watches a module that is not installed
body:
The `http: vault` monitor points at `https://vault.$DOMAIN`, but the `vault` module is not in `enabled_modules` in `wizard.state` — no container, no route — so it can only ever be down. That is a *not installed* module, not a tailnet-only route (see GUIDE "Module state vs route exposure").

**Fix (operator, in the Kuma UI — an agent must not write to a user service):** install the vault module, or pause/delete the monitor. Nothing in the repo needs to change.

title: Kuma config copy from the old machine is blocked
body:
SSH to the old box denies every key tried from the app host, Tailscale SSH is not enabled there and its Taildrop inbox is empty, so the old `kuma.db` cannot be fetched; kuma.$DOMAIN currently has only the seeded admin (reset Aug 2026).

**Fix:** on the operator's Mac run `ssh-keygen -R <old box tailnet IP>`, then `ssh debian@<IP>`; deliver the db by taildrop or by adding the app host's key, then `make kuma-import` (adapts URLs, container names and deactivates retired-service monitors).

See `docs/ISSUES.md` (frozen archive) for the full detail.

title: A vanished module is never recreated at boot
body:
`deployed()` in `scripts/stack/stack-up.sh` gates on *container existence*, so when a module's containers are gone (image prune, `compose down`, docker storage wipe) boot recovery logs `skip (not deployed)` — the stack reports "up" while the module is silently absent.

**Fix:** treat `wizard.state`'s `enabled_modules` as the source of truth for a module the installer deployed, and recreate any module whose compose file exists but whose containers are missing.

title: The optimize offer is marked broken in the installer
body:
`ask_optimize` (`scripts/install/wizard.d/flow/optimize.sh`) carries a `## BROKEN — neither prompt answer fires optimize.sh` marker from an earlier run, yet the wiring looks correct, so the marker has never been reproduced or traced.

**Fix:** on the next green operator run answer `yes` and confirm optimize.sh starts; if it does, delete the marker; if not, trace `ask_boolean`'s `printf -v` target from that call site.

title: Most ops and module scripts have no dry-run or plan mode
body:
AGENTS rule 29 lets an agent exercise a script only through a dry/plan mode or a fixture target; apart from `optimize.sh --dry-run` and `restore-data.sh`'s preview, `scripts/ops/*` and `scripts/modules/*` have neither, so a change to them cannot be verified without a real run.

**Fix (candidate, not approved):** add a `DRYRUN=1` path that prints the plan and exits before the first mutation, starting with the scripts that write state (`talk-gen.sh`, `nc-capture.sh`, `stack-up.sh`).

title: Destructive make recipes run with no confirmation guard
body:
Several recipes destroy data or overwrite live state with no prompt and no automatic backup: `nc-user-del`/`mail-del`/`kuma-del-user`, `nc-datadir-nfs`, `install-config`, `update`, `dok-recreate-all`/`dok-stop-all`/`dok-recreate-nextcloud-db`.

**Fix:** pick a policy — a `CONFIRM=1` gate on the destructive recipes, or keep them unguarded and list them explicitly in `make help-more` (today they are not in one obvious list). Changes recipe UX, so it needs an operator decision.

title: PHP sessions live in a non-persistent Redis
body:
`modules/nextcloud/docker-compose.yml` runs redis with `--save "" --appendonly no`, and the image entrypoint stores PHP sessions there — a redis restart/recreate (or eviction) logs every user out.

**Fix:** accept, or give redis minimal RDB persistence so sessions survive a restart.

title: NFS datadirectory: hard mount + sync export + no_root_squash
body:
A `sync` export over the tailnet is the write-latency bottleneck (the 2026-09-10 migration stalled at ~227 KB/s); `hard` means a storage outage blocks Nextcloud I/O with no timeout escape; `no_root_squash` lets any tailnet host write as root on the export.

**Fix:** consider `async` (faster, weaker crash durability) and root-squashing — both change behaviour and need an explicit operator decision.

title: No automated validation of the scripts
body:
Only `make smoke` and the git hooks run; nothing lints the large bash scripts that produced two bugs on 2026-09-10 (`nc-datadir-nfs.sh`, `optimize.sh`).

**Fix:** run `bash -n` + `shellcheck` over `scripts/**` on the pushed range. The natural home is a CI workflow on pull requests — CI is deliberately not implemented yet (see the monitoring/CI discussion), so the interim step is a pre-push addition.

title: talk-hpb was OOM-killed
body:
`journalctl` shows the kernel OOM-killing nextcloud-spreed-signaling on 2026-09-09 under the stack's RAM cap (`modules/nextcloud/docker-compose.yml`).

**Fix:** confirm recurrence; raise the cap or reduce concurrency if it repeats.

title: GUIDE "Nextcloud DB" still documents moving PostgreSQL to the 1 TB machine
body:
Setup A keeps PostgreSQL on the app host and puts only Nextcloud's user files on the 1 TB machine, but `docs/GUIDE.md` still gives step-by-step instructions to move the whole DB there, and the `docker-compose.db.yml` comments are tuned for "the 2 GB future DB host". One of the two is the plan.

**Fix:** operator decision — delete the migration steps (Setup A won) or re-document them as an option.

title: A fresh install has no www.$DOMAIN homepage
body:
Pages are instance data only (`$DATA_DIR/pages/www`, the repo ships none), so on a fresh install `/` matches the `@index` handle and `file_server` answers 404 until the operator drops an `index.html` there — the smoke's www check then fails on an otherwise-finished install.

**Fix:** operator adds `index.html` to `$DATA_DIR/pages/www`; alternatively have the installer seed a minimal placeholder only when the tree is empty.

title: Caddy edge lacks rate + connection limiting
body:
Every public vhost reverse-proxies an upstream with no `ratelimit` or `connlimit` guard, so a single client (or botnet) can exhaust any upstream's resources via `wss://`, sync or repeated API calls.

**Fix:** add site-level `connlimit` or a global `ratelimit` per vhost; consider rate-limiting `/signaling` and Kuma's admin routes. Files: `modules/caddy/Caddyfile` + the per-vhost files.

title: Fail2ban covers sshd only — no web-app login jails
body:
`config/fail2ban/jail.d/` ships only `sshd.conf`, so Nextcloud/Talk/Roundcube/Vaultwarden/Kuma login pages have no jail — an attacker can hammer app password endpoints from one IP.

**Fix:** add per-app jails (nextcloud, vaultwarden, roundcube, kuma) pointing at each app's login route.

title: goose server secret is in git history
body:
The installer used to `sed` a generated `GOOSE_SERVER__SECRET_KEY` into the tracked unit, so a real key sits in git history. The repo now uses `EnvironmentFile=$DATA_DIR/goose/.env` (0600), but the old value is still in history and unrotated.

**Fix:** rotate the key (new value in `data/goose/.env`, `systemctl restart goose`, update clients), then purge it from history if desired. Rotation restarts the agent service; a history purge needs a force-push.

title: `curl … | sh` in the installers
body:
Piping a remote script into a shell is supply-chain exposure; the installer does it for tailscale and goose, and `scripts/ops/nc-datadir-nfs.sh` for tailscale.

**Fix:** use the official Tailscale apt repo (keyring + sources.list + `apt-get install`); keep the vendor's goose installer (or verify a released binary) and note the exception.

title: `make backup` copies live config into the repo
body:
`make backup` copies live host configs into `$(REPO)/repo/config/`; if one carries a secret, the next `git add` commits it (the goose unit did exactly this until 2026-09-11). The pull also resurrects *scrubbed* content — a stale live `/etc/sysctl.d/99-<hostname>.conf` re-imported a banned name the repo had deliberately removed.

**Fix:** keep secrets in dedicated files outside the copied set; optionally add a secret-scan guard to the pre-commit hook. After `make backup`, `git diff config/` before any `git add`.

title: Mail platform: PTR record does not resolve to mail.$DOMAIN
body:
Inbound TCP 25 is open and postfix serves the LE cert, but the reverse record for `$SERVER_IP` points at the hosting provider's own hostname — outbound mail to Gmail/Outlook is rejected or spam-foldered until it matches. The reverse zone belongs to the provider.

**Fix (operator, ~2 min):** in the provider's control panel set the PTR for `$SERVER_IP` to `mail.$DOMAIN` (it must match the postfix HELO and the A record), verify with `dig -x $SERVER_IP`, then send a test to an external inbox.

title: Tailscale tailnet has 2 stale devices
body:
`kaliusb` (linux, 18d offline) and `iosphone` (iOS, 6h offline) are still registered; stale devices widen the ACL blast radius.

**Fix:** in the Tailscale admin console remove both, or rename and tag them if still in use.

title: Tailscale ACLs not configured
body:
`ts-input` accepts all tailnet traffic, so any added device reaches every open port on the machine.

**Fix:** in the Tailscale admin console restrict which devices/tags can reach this machine.

title: Rotate the exposed GitHub PAT
body:
The PAT that lived in `.git/config` `origin` is compromised — it was in git history before the purge. The remote and the history are gone, but the token value was exposed.

**Fix:** revoke it at https://github.com/settings/tokens (or confirm it expired). PAT usage is dropped entirely in favour of SSH.

title: Nextcloud 2FA not enforced
body:
The setup check reports second-factor providers are available but two-factor authentication is not enforced — any stolen password alone grants access.

**Fix (operator):** configure a TOTP provider on the account, then `occ twofactorauth:enforce admin` (or `--all`). Enforcing before the provider exists can lock the account out.

title: Nextcloud default phone region not set
body:
`default_phone_region` is unset, so profile phone numbers without a country code cannot be validated (the setup check warns).

**Fix (operator):** `occ config:system:set default_phone_region --value <ISO-3166-1-ALPHA-2>` — the country code is the operator's to pick.

title: PHP-FPM pool sizing under concurrent sync
body:
`modules/nextcloud/php-fpm.d/zz-custom.conf` runs `pm.max_children = 8` with a 200 s terminate timeout, so slow syncs can occupy every child (already switched to `ondemand`, so idle workers free at rest).

**Fix:** monitor `docker stats nextcloud` / `occ status`; raise `max_children` only if sync load grows, lower `request_terminate_timeout` if 504s appear.

title: Stop goose when idle
body:
The goose agent service (`goose serve`) holds memory idle when no session is active. It is protected by the AGENTS safety rules (must not be deleted), but a temporary `systemctl stop` between sessions would free RAM.

**Fix:** `systemctl stop goose` when unused, `systemctl start goose` before a session — an operator convenience trade-off (cold start latency vs idle RAM).

title: Nextcloud Talk: no Client Push proxy
body:
Mobile push notifications are delayed — no push proxy (UnifiedPush / nextcloud-push) is installed. The signalling side is fine: the Go HPB (`talk-hpb`) has run since the 2026-08-30 rebuild.

**Fix:** install a push proxy plus the Notifications backend when Talk push becomes a real use case.

title: `goose session remove` cannot prune sessions
body:
`goose session remove --regex <re>` lists the matching sessions and then fails with `Error: not connected` — the CLI drives removal through the running `goose serve` ACP endpoint and the handshake never succeeds, so the store (which has no retention) can only be trimmed out-of-band.

**Fix:** prune `~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db` with python3 (delete `messages` + `usage_ledger` by `session_id`, then the `sessions` row; keep the live session) — procedure in the goose token bullet of `docs/GUIDE.md`. Re-test after a goose upgrade.

title: Auto-compaction has never been observed firing
body:
The token policy is settled (goose validates the threshold as `>0 … ≤1`), but no session has been driven past it, so what built-in compaction actually sends and whether the session is continued or forked is untested.

**Fix:** drive one session past the configured threshold (or set a deliberately tiny fraction once) and confirm in `~/.local/state/goose/logs/llm_request.*.jsonl` that the transcript is replaced by a summary inside the same session id.

title: Talk relay and Snikket coturn both want 3478/5349
body:
Snikket's coturn is on 3478/5349 (standard ports, advertised via XEP-0215) and `talk-relay` publishes the same two, so only one can bind them — re-enabling the Talk stack stops Snikket's TURN from starting. The relay ranges do not overlap (Talk 49160-49200, Snikket 49201-65535).

**Fix:** give talk-relay its own listener pair (e.g. 3481 plain + 5351 TLS) in the compose published ports, `modules/nextcloud/talk/turnserver.conf.example`, the installer's `occ talk:turn:add` values and `03-firewall.sh`, then regenerate the live turnserver.conf with `make talk-gen` — or keep Talk off.

title: New modules are outside the backup/restore universe
body:
`scripts/ops/backup-bundles.sh` and `scripts/ops/restore-data.sh` list `vault mailserver kuma` explicitly, so the `home`, `blog` and `photos` datadirs are neither bundled nor restorable.

**Fix:** derive the datadir universe from `config/modules.conf` (one loop over `mod_all`/`mod_dir`) instead of extending the literals.

title: social.$DOMAIN — Mastodon (or the minimal fediverse alternative)
body:
A fediverse presence has been considered but not approved — do not start without the operator's go-ahead.

**Decision needed:** Mastodon (5 containers, ~1.2–1.8 GB added idle, full-featured) vs GoToSocial (single Go binary, SQLite, ~60 MB, same ActivityPub network).

**If built (either way):** a new `social` module — compose file, data under `$DATA_DIR` on local disk, SMTP via the mailserver (`social@$DOMAIN`, the `mail-gen` pattern), CF-proxied A record + LE DNS-01, Kuma monitor, smoke section, fetch row, installer/uninstaller hooks, and memory limits from day one.

title: NC user isolation across apps
body:
Keep Nextcloud users isolated from each other (own groups) across the apps they touch.

**Reality check:** mail, Nextcloud and Vaultwarden each have separate user models — full cross-app isolation needs per-app groups, consistent naming and a documented matrix; true SSO-style isolation is a bigger architecture question. Spike/design before committing.
